Three renderer capture runs of the example produced the same bytes for the idle and aborted frames and different bytes for the other four, whose URL line shows the ephemeral port of the loopback server.
The suite passed 9 of 9 runs under 14 busy loops on the 11-core machine (6 before the commit and 3 from the committed tree), and passes with the control receipts absent, as in CI.

limits: WebSocket is the next slice: the global is RN's and fails on first use with 'WebSocketModule' could not be found, and BlobModule's socket methods throw E_UNSUPPORTED.
Cookies are neither stored nor sent: withCredentials has no effect and clearCookies calls back false. OkHttp and NSURLSession keep a cookie jar.

A response with a Content-Encoding other than identity fails explicitly (OkHttp and NSURLSession decode it); a string request body with Content-Encoding gzip also fails, and that path has no check of its own.
The body is buffered and delivered once: no incremental text updates, no upload or download progress events; a 1 MiB body arrives over several budgeted polls.
uri bodies and FormData file parts fail explicitly; PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE and PATCH map to Godot's client with no check of their own.

HTTP/1.1, one connection per request: no pooling, keep-alive, HTTP/2, proxy configuration or system trust configuration; outside the validation seam TLS trusts Godot's roots, with no revocation or pinning.
The contract is Android's: RN's iOS wrapper would need a second native module over another spec; failure texts are this host's, not OkHttp's; BlobModule's constants are iOS's.
The react-native facade gains no export: Networking stays missing, and the globals are RN's own.
Only macOS arm64 was executed: Godot Android (INTERNET permission), iOS and Web (CORS) exports, hardware, offline and reconnect behavior are not covered.
GF-22 is open: only its first-slice checkpoint closes, and no whole GF, other checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closes.

causes.finding: A late answer or error could replace the view of a newer request, and a second Slow left the first request in flight where Abort could not reach it
The text step was checked only through the screen: nothing asserted from the server's log that exactly one GET reached /api/text

causes.source: CodeRabbit on PR #47, scripts/networking-sabotage.mjs (the same pattern in the three other sabotage scripts)
causes.finding: The sabotaged sources were restored only in finally blocks, which do not run when SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the process, so an interrupted build could leave a broken native source in the tree
stopServer always waited for a new exit event, so a server that had already crashed hung the suite until the job timeout, and a closed stdin pipe could raise an unhandled EPIPE

The timeout of run sent SIGTERM to the child's process group once and never escalated, so a child (or a grandchild holding the output pipes) that ignores SIGTERM kept the call pending and the script hung with the sabotaged source in the tree

changes.example: A late answer or error is logged but no longer replaces the view of a newer request (the newest request owns the screen), a second Slow aborts the previous slow request, and the validation also checks from the server's log that the text step sent exactly one GET to /api/text
changes.sabotageScripts: scripts/sabotage-sources.mjs swaps and restores the sources, checks the restored hashes, and runs the builds and the probes as awaited children in process groups of their own; on SIGINT or SIGTERM it forwards the signal to the group, waits for the children (SIGKILL after 5 s, at once on a second signal), restores the sources synchronously and exits with 128 plus the signal; all four sabotage scripts use it and their receipts keep their formats
changes.runner: stopServer resolves at once for a child whose exitCode or signalCode is set and ignores an error on its stdin
changes.sabotageTimeout: the timeout of run in scripts/sabotage-sources.mjs sends SIGTERM to the child's group and SIGKILL after the same 5 s grace period as on a signal; both timers are cleared when the child closes, so a child past its timeout comes back with status null instead of the script waiting on it

timeoutFix.note: Run on the tree that holds D's helper, with the SHA-256 pinned above
runs: A scratch harness over temporary files (outside the repository) with 14 scenarios, five of them new for the timeout of run: a child that ignores SIGTERM under a 300 ms timeout, a child whose grandchild ignores SIGTERM and holds the output pipes, a child that obeys it, a child that handles it itself a second later, and a SIGINT during the grace period. Before the fix 12 pass and 2 fail (the first two: the script was still waiting for the child after 15 s, with the source still sabotaged). After it 14 pass: run returns after 5.3 s (300 ms plus the 5 s grace period) with the child killed, the source is restored and no process is left
A variant of the fix that does not clear the escalation timer is rejected by two scenarios: the script lives 5.4 s after its last line instead of 0.4 s and 1.4 s
